MATHEMATICS — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #16
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which expression shows "6 less than k"? (1 mark)
   A. k + 6
   B. 6 − k
   C. 6k
   D. k − 6

2. Kip faces South and makes a quarter turn anticlockwise. Which way does he face now? (1 mark)
   A. South
   B. East
   C. West
   D. North

3. What is 1/10 of 50? (1 mark)
   A. 5
   B. 10
   C. 11
   D. 45

4. Which of these shows 583 in words? (1 mark)
   A. five hundred and eighty-three
   B. five hundred and thirty-eight
   C. six hundred and eighty-three
   D. five hundred and ninety-three

5. On an analogue clock the short hour hand has reached or passed the number 8 but not yet reached the next number, and the long minute hand points to the number 10. What time is shown? (1 mark)
   A. 8:10
   B. 10:40
   C. 8:50
   D. 9:50

6. Which statement about a rectangle is true? (1 mark)
   A. Opposite sides are equal and all corners are right angles
   B. It has three sides
   C. All sides are always equal
   D. It has a curved edge

7. Cuboid A is 6 by 2 by 2 blocks (length, width, height). Cuboid B is 3 by 3 by 3 blocks. Which has the greater volume? (1 mark)
   A. Cuboid A
   B. It cannot be told
   C. Cuboid B
   D. They are equal

8. How many quarter turns make a half turn? (1 mark)
   A. 4
   B. 2
   C. 3
   D. 1

9. The table shows the pets kept by 10 families: dog 3, cat 3, rabbit 2, hen 2. How many are dog or hen together? (1 mark)
   A. 3
   B. 5
   C. 4
   D. 6

10. The table shows the favourite colours of 10 pupils: blue 4, red 4, green 2. How many are blue or green together? (1 mark)
   A. 5
   B. 7
   C. 6
   D. 4

11. Which statement about 2,908 is correct? (1 mark)
   A. It is odd because it ends in 8
   B. It is odd because it has an even number of digits
   C. It is neither even nor odd
   D. It is even because it ends in 8

12. How many 1/4 L cups can be filled from 3 L of milk? (1 mark)
   A. 12
   B. 7
   C. 9
   D. 6

13. A quarter turn makes (1 mark)
   A. a full turn
   B. no angle
   C. a right angle
   D. a straight line

14. What is 3 1/4 kg + 2 1/2 kg? (1 mark)
   A. 5 1/2 kg
   B. 6 1/4 kg
   C. 5 3/4 kg
   D. 6 kg

15. What is 75 cm in metres? (1 mark)
   A. 0.075 m
   B. 0.75 m
   C. 75 m
   D. 7.5 m

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. A shop earned Ksh 4,750 on Monday and Ksh 3,895 on Tuesday. How much did it earn on the two days? (3 marks)

17. The minute hand of a clock points to 4 and the hour hand is just past 9. What time is it? Explain how you know. (3 marks)

18. Mama Njoki has 24 oranges. She gives 3/8 of them to her neighbours and 1/4 of them to a friend. (a) How many oranges does she give to her neighbours? (b) How many does she give to her friend? (c) How many oranges are left? (5 marks)

19. The table shows mango 4, banana 3, orange 2 and pawpaw 1. How many pupils did not choose mango? (2 marks)

20. A tank has 50 L of water. The family uses 18 L. How much water is left? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #16 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — k − 6
   The key words tell us the operation. "6 less than k" is written k − 6.

2. B — East
   Going clockwise the order is North, East, South, West. Going anticlockwise it is North, West, South, East. South followed by a quarter turn anticlockwise gives East.

3. A — 5
   50 ÷ 10 = 5 and 5 × 1 = 5. So 1/10 of 50 is 5.

4. A — five hundred and eighty-three
   583 = five hundred and eighty-three. Say the hundreds, then "and", then the tens and ones.

5. C — 8:50
   Each number on the clock face is worth 5 minutes. The minute hand at 10 shows 10 × 5 = 50 minutes, so the time is 8:50.

6. A — Opposite sides are equal and all corners are right angles
   A rectangle has four sides, opposite sides equal and four right angles.

7. C — Cuboid B
   A = 6 × 2 × 2 = 24 blocks. B = 3 × 3 × 3 = 27 blocks. Cuboid B is greater.

8. B — 2
   Two quarters make a half.

9. B — 5
   3 + 2 = 5.

10. C — 6
   4 + 2 = 6.

11. D — It is even because it ends in 8
   Look at the ones digit. 8 is even, so 2,908 is even.

12. A — 12
   Each litre fills 4 cups, so 3 L fills 3 × 4 = 12 cups.

13. C — a right angle
   A quarter turn sweeps out a right angle.

14. C — 5 3/4 kg
   Work with the whole kilograms first and then the parts. 3 1/4 kg + 2 1/2 kg = 5 3/4 kg.

15. B — 0.75 m
   1 m = 100 cm. Use this to change between the two units: 75 cm in metres is 0.75 m.

SECTION B
----
16. (3 marks)
   Answer: Ksh 8,645
   Working / marking points: 4,750 + 3,895. Ones 5; tens 5 + 9 = 14 write 4 carry 1; hundreds 7 + 8 + 1 = 16 write 6 carry 1; thousands 4 + 3 + 1 = 8. 1 mark for setting up, 1 for regrouping, 1 for the answer with units.

17. (3 marks)
   Answer: 9:20. Each number is worth 5 minutes, so the minute hand at 4 shows 4 × 5 = 20 minutes past 9.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 9:20, 1 mark for 5 minutes per number, 1 mark for 4 × 5.

18. (5 marks)
   Answer: (a) 9 oranges (b) 6 oranges (c) 9 oranges
   Working / marking points: (a) 24 ÷ 8 = 3, 3 × 3 = 9 (2 marks); (b) 24 ÷ 4 = 6 (1 mark); (c) 24 − 9 − 6 = 9 (2 marks).

19. (2 marks)
   Answer: 6 pupils
   Working / marking points: 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 10 pupils; 10 − 4 = 6 (1 mark for the total, 1 mark for the answer).

20. (2 marks)
   Answer: 32 L
   Working / marking points: 50 − 18 = 32. 1 mark for the subtraction and 1 mark for the unit.
